Daily Briefing — Thursday, May 14 2026

Enterprise AI Governance and Orchestration Emerge as Critical Battleground as Boomi and Goldman Sachs Sound Urgent ROI Warning

AI & Technology

#1 — Boomi Expands Platform with AI Agent Governance and Orchestration Tools — IT Brief Asia

★ Direct relevance to Cristiano's AI governance strategy—Boomi's new capabilities for agent connectivity, agentic workflows, and controlled data access align with his needs for operationalizing AI agents in financial services contexts.

Boomi has expanded its enterprise platform with new tools for managing AI agents, data and workflow orchestration, with a focus on governance and control. The additions span governed agent connectivity, orchestrated agentic workflows, agentic engineering, grounded agent context and localised agent infrastructure. Boomi's Connect product offers managed links through more than 1,000 MCP-enabled tools, while its AI Gateway adds policy enforcement, spending controls and monitoring.

Financial Services Technology

#2 — Large Language Model Market Projected to Reach $823.93 Billion by 2040 — Research and Markets

★ Market sizing and trajectory data for strategic planning: LLM market expansion at 35.57% CAGR validates long-term positioning of LLM-driven enterprise solutions, particularly in financial content operations.

The global large language model (LLM) market is poised to grow from USD 11.63 billion this year to USD 823.93 billion by 2040, driven by a CAGR of 35.57%. Industries like healthcare, BFSI, and IT & telecommunications are embracing multimodal LLM technologies to automate processes. Tech giants like Microsoft, Amazon, Baidu, Luma AI, and Meta are investing in model innovation, accelerating adoption across sectors.

Executive Leadership & Strategy

#1 — Enterprise AI Adoption Faces Structural Challenges: 79% Report Difficulties Despite Investment — Writer

★ Executive context for positioning: Writer's 2026 survey of 2,400 C-suite leaders reveals a crisis of execution—97% see AI benefits but only 29% achieve organizational ROI, highlighting the governance and orchestration gap Cristiano should address in his CPTO narrative.

The 2026 survey findings reveal 79% of organizations face challenges in adopting AI, with 54% of C-suite executives admitting that adopting AI is tearing their company apart. The shift toward agentic AI has moved at a pace that's hard to overstate. Nearly all executives (97%) say their company deployed AI agents in the past year, with 52% of employees already using them.

#2 — AI Governance Gap Requires Urgent 90-Day Execution Framework — Help Net Security

★ Strategic leadership framework: SurePath AI CEO outlines the governance gap endemic to enterprises and proposes a structured remediation approach—visibility, policy, and operational auditing—directly applicable to Cristiano's CPTO positioning.

AI adoption is outpacing governance maturity by a wide margin, creating friction between security teams pushing for responsible use and business leaders worried about falling behind competitors. Typical audits reveal shadow AI use, sensitive data moving into models without checks, and agentic workflows operating with broad system access. A 90-day framework spans discovery and visibility in the first month, policy and guardrails in the second, and operational auditing in the third.
